script: In 1925, a con artist named Victor Lustig read a newspaper article about the Eiffel Tower needing expensive repairs, and got an insane idea. He printed fake government letterhead, posed as a French official, and secretly invited six scrap metal dealers to a luxury hotel. He told them the tower was going to be torn down and sold for scrap, and the sale had to stay secret to avoid public outrage. One dealer paid him a fortune to win the bid. Lustig took the cash and vanished to Vienna before anyone realized the Eiffel Tower was never for sale at all. The victim was too embarrassed to go to the police. Lustig liked the con so much, he came back to Paris and sold the tower again to a different buyer.
